item.title: [47. Russian International Affairs Council (RIAC) --Russia] Why the West Still Misunderstands BRICS
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在47. Russian International Affairs Council (RIAC) --Russia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Why the West Still Misunderstands BRICS

发布源: 47. Russian International Affairs Council (RIAC) --Russia | 抓取时间: 2026-10-10

Login if you are already registered

President of the Russian International Affairs Council

Short versionof the article

Full versionof the article

When the BRIC group, as it was known then, first emerged, it was greeted with amusement as another exotic variety of alphabet soup in the age of globalization. As it became a more permanent fixture, it was regarded as a poor man’s version of a global club, like a humble answer to the G7.

More recently, it has come to be feared, not least by US President Donald Trump, as a potential threat to the dominance of the American dollar. In the run-up to the 2026 BRICS summit in New Delhi, the Western media shifted its focus to the divergences within the group, essentially portraying it as something less than the sum of its parts.

However, all these interpretations miss the actual significance of BRICS, which is its role as an early model of the emerging multipolar order.

Its members vary enormously in population, territory, economic weight, military strength and technological and scientific capabilities and their histories aren’t as closely intertwined as those of Europe and North America, while their political systems are highly diverse and their domestic and foreign policies often point in different directions.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在32. Gaidar Institute for Economic Policy, FKA Institute for the Economy in Transition --Russia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Monitoring legal regulation of the digital economy

发布源: 32. Gaidar Institute for Economic Policy, FKA Institute for the Economy in Transition --Russia | 抓取时间: 2026-10-10

Starting from 2024, Gaidar Institute launched a monthly review of international trends in the legal regulation of the digital economy. The purpose of Monitoring is to timely identify key developments and trends in the global practice of regulating the digital sector. The scientific and expert analysis allows not only to track current changes, but also to forecast their potential impact on the development of the digital industry in our country, contributing to the formation of an adaptive and effective strategy of legal regulation in this area.

It is published in Russian and English.
